primary_frame: Regression: predict employee performance_rating from workplace and experience features
alternative_frames: Classification: bin performance_rating into tiers and predict tier membership
Feature importance: identify which employee attributes most associate with performance
Classification: predict salary_band from employee and workplace features
Segmentation: cluster employees by work-arrangement features and compare performance
required_checks: Compute pairwise correlations between all numeric features and performance_rating
Test whether any predictor explains significant variance in performance_rating beyond chance
Run a baseline regression and compare R-squared to a null (permuted-target) model
Check commute_minutes for outliers and right-skew impact on model assumptions
Verify salary_band levels have distinct feature profiles before treating as ordinal
Assess multicollinearity among predictors before fitting multivariate models
framing_risks: Performance_rating distribution (mean ~50, std ~10) is consistent with pure random noise; predictive models may find no real signal
No target variable is explicitly labeled; choosing performance_rating as outcome is an assumption
Dataset may be entirely synthetic with independent columns, making any fitted model spurious
800 rows with 9 predictors is large enough to produce nominally significant but meaningless correlations
Salary_band top-frequency is L5 (170/800) but level ordering and meaning are unknown
